Transaction originated from a new unrecognized device profile (Trident/7.0 | Windows 8.1 | ie 11.0 for )

case.summary: The investigation concludes that transaction 3464869 was a confirmed compromise, not an authorized cardholder purchase, resulting in a total exposure of $599.94 under the “card‑not‑present new‑device” pattern. Evidence includes the single flagged transaction on Card C03042‑K1, the absence of any linked cards, and the detection of a new, unrecognized device profile consistent with fraudulent CNP activity. Accordingly, the card has been blocked for re‑issuance and a fraud case has been created per bank policy.

evidence_requests.assumed_response: Customer states they did not recognize the charge and have not shared their card credentials.

initial.reason: R1: Elevated fraud probability on flagged authorization; decline pending inquiry
R1: Require step-up passcode/auth before allowing further activity

final.reason: R2: Customer denied transaction; open case and record to graph

next_best_actions.what_changed: Customer denial confirmed unauthorized transaction, elevating fraud probability to 0.95. Pre-evidence monitoring escalated to immediate BLOCK_CARD and CREATE_CASE under Policy R2. Because exposure ($599.94) is under $1,000 and no cross-card compromise linkage exists, the matter is resolved as case-only without external regulatory SAR filing.

sar.reason: No regulatory filing required under Fraud Policy thresholds (exposure under limit and no multi-account ring link).

stop_reason: Definitive evidence of compromise obtained; protective actions and report executed.
